newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midco gasoline seen firming on Clark order.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midco gasoline seen firming on Clark order.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline differentials were expected to firm following a court ruling that idled two processing units at a key regional refinery for another two weeks, traders said late Monday.

An Illinois judge ordered Clark Refining and Marketing Co not to restart a propane scrubber and 6,400 barrel per day alkylation unit at its 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., refinery until at least November 8 because of safety concerns at the plant.
"Gasoline should firm on this, although it wasn't totally unexpected and Clark has been covering" a Chicago trader said.

The Illinois Attorney General sought a court order shutting the Blue Island refinery following three headline-grabbing accidents over the past 18 months. The most recent was a fire on October 19 that idled the alkylation unit.

Clark said the refinery was running safely and operations have improved since an accident that killed two workers and a release of fumes that made more than two dozen students sick at a nearby high school last year.

A Clark spokeswoman was not immediately available for comment on the court order. The independent refiner and marketer operates three U.S. refineries supplying gasoline and refined products to a network of 830 gasoline stations and convenience stores.

Earlier in the day, talk of heavy buying by Amoco Corp in the U.S. Gulf Coast fueled higher futures and cash prices, with the support spilling over into differentials in Chicago and Group Three markets, traders said.

Amoco told regulators a valve failed, causing an operational upset in a fluid catalytic cracker at its 433,000 barrel per day Texas City, Texas refinery. The Chicago-based company declined comment on the incident.
